gaps.title: XML PUT parser, checksum errors and commit cancellation boundaries remain local
gaps.observed_evidence: The PUT method requires Content-Length unless chunked, defines replacement, Content-MD5 InvalidDigest/BadDigest, and returns empty 200. The headers reference defines octet-stream serving fallback, 8 KiB custom metadata and big-endian CRC32C; IAM requires create plus delete for overwrite. Local PUT uses the existing JSON bounded bridge and transactional publication/recovery. Configured size excess returns XML 400 EntityTooLarge, missing framing 411 MissingContentLength, malformed/conflicting hash declarations 400 InvalidDigest including CRC32C, and any supplied checksum mismatch 400 BadDigest. The status catalog separately names InvalidCrc; precise CRC-specific errors remain a declared deviation. HTTP names normalize to lowercase; duplicate fixed/precondition/custom fields return 400 ExcessHeaderValues, empty custom suffixes and non-ASCII values return 400 InvalidArgument, and the metadata cap counts stored suffix/value bytes as shared storage does, rather than the HTTP prefix. Empty optional fixed values clear those fields; omitted content type is stored as application/octet-stream. Hyper owns transport-invalid framing and automatic 100-continue; trailers are explicitly unsupported, announced trailers fail before body reads and unannounced trailer frames abort without publication. Unknown query/x-goog inputs follow SPEC-XML-INPUTS 501; all x-amz extensions also fail 501. Retry tokens need generation match and have no response replay. Existing local XML path/ETag/auth/permission-precedence choices remain SPEC-XML-PREFIX/PATH-ERROR/INPUTS, SPEC-012 and SPEC-017. Complete bodies may finish publication after response timeout, disconnect or shutdown; only pre-EOF interruption guarantees no publication. Rust wire cases verify 13 scoped behaviors and recovery without claiming provider differential parity, every fsync crash boundary, power loss, measured RSS/cgroup bounds or actual-browser signed transfers.
gaps.required_resolution: Keep EXT-XML-022 PARTIAL. Implement signing/payload verification, ACLs, encryption, requester billing, class overrides, retention/explicit holds, custom time, copy/resumable/multipart variants and other advanced inputs in their owning slices. Establish authoritative or explicitly authorized provider evidence for duplicate/non-ASCII/metadata-size accounting, hash conflict and CRC-specific errors, mixed-error ordering, framing/trailers and complete response headers. Preserve bounded streaming and atomic create/delete/condition checks, and never promise rollback of a commit already running after EOF. Run integrated signed-browser/container/SDK gates separately; Go storage v1.70.0 writes JSON Objects.Insert, so these XML PUT cases use Rust raw HTTP rather than claiming SDK write coverage. Source digests, exact scope and final commands are in docs/en/slices/xml-put-object.md and docs/en/evidence/xml-put-object.md.

The provider does not enumerate the complete JSON exposed-common-header set or document custom iOS-scheme/null acceptance exhaustively. Local scope fixes a standard common-header subset including ETag/Location/Range/Content-Range, supports serialized capacitor/ionic/custom origins and null without an HTTP-only allowlist, and bounds minified stored CORS to 64 KiB. gaps.required_resolution: Retain these provider/device questions outside the frozen tested local scope. Keep custom-origin wire handling distinct from actual WebKit emission, native bridge success and cookie identity. gaps.title: Resumable error, total, checksum and terminal-session edge parity needs independent evidence
gaps.observed_evidence: Sources establish seven-day lifetime, persisted-prefix immutability, 308/Range with no Range for zero persisted bytes, unknown totals, final 200/201 and JSON cancellation 499. The concept page gives 410 for an invalid URI before one week and 404 after one week; the performing guide promises only a future 4xx after cancellation. They do not establish exact deadline equality, cancellation-repeat/completed-DELETE body shape, failed-session retention, zero-body bytes */N finalization distinction, total/header conflict errors, offset-gap or concurrent-writer errors, chunk alignment enforcement, final custom-metadata key conflicts, or MIME precedence when metadata conflicts with X-Upload-Content-Type. Local choices are 604800 seconds with expiry at equality, cancelled-session 410 before deadline and 404 at/after, completed-session DELETE 410 before expiry, and committed cancellation 499 even if physical cleanup fails, with visible journaled cleanup retried by maintenance. Other local choices are bounded completed-resource retention, 400 malformed/gap/total errors, 503 concurrent-writer/admission rejection, complete-request offset checkpoints, and metadata contentType before X-Upload-Content-Type. Pinned Go sends an empty final POST with bytes */offset for an exact chunk multiple and whole-object CRC32C in final X-Goog-Hash. The general concept page recommends Content-MD5, whereas JSON-specific validation documents final X-Goog-Hash; Content-MD5 stays explicitly unsupported in the existing local JSON profile. Checked official JSON sources do not define fake-gcs-server's alternate x-goog-upload-* command protocol. On 2026-10-23, objects.insert and data-validation were rechecked for the basic contract: the subsequent-PUT statement uses the words these headers while introducing query parameters; whether it means condition queries remains unresolved, while local session requests reject extra queries with 400 (wire-tested for PUT ifGenerationMatch). This named chunk-query rejection deviation and finalization recheck timing are retained under SPEC-RSM-AUTH-CONDITIONS and JSON-OBJECTS-007-PENDING, not promoted BEHAVIOR-COMMON-011 evidence. Data-validation documents final whole-object X-Goog-Hash but excludes MD5 validation for chunked objects without explicitly resolving multi-request JSON resumable uploads. Local multi-request resumable MD5 calculation, exposure and validation remain source-uncertain under this gap; they do not contribute to the promoted BEHAVIOR-OBJECT-005 scope. No real-service differential test was run.
gaps.required_resolution: Keep the exact supported subset and explicit local choices in docs/en/slices/resumable-upload.md; never claim provider error/edge parity from local tests. Local committed terminal validation failures preserve their original error response when physical cleanup fails; diagnostics and the deletion journal retain the cleanup failure for maintenance retry, and successful cleanup is not repeated before expiry. Obtain authoritative clarification or explicitly authorized cloud evidence for error bodies/order, invalid-session lifetime boundaries, completed/failed session retention, status versus empty finalization, length/total conflicts, concurrent/invalid chunks, metadata/header precedence, Content-MD5 and alternate upload command applicability. Keep x-goog-upload command variants outside the verified slice and reject recognized unsupported semantics. Completed-session protocol state is separate from SPEC-013 token-keyed response replay. Preserve local RSM-FINAL-004/005 PASS evidence and add explicit JSON-OBJECTS-007-PENDING parity wording for stored-condition finalization timing and extra-query 400 (wire-tested for PUT ifGenerationMatch) versus the ambiguous subsequent-PUT ignoring wording; SPEC-RSM-AUTH-CONDITIONS owns that reconciliation and SPEC-008 owns mutation NotMatch 412. Retain multi-data-request resumable MD5 as a named source question on JSON-OBJECTS-007-PENDING until authoritative evidence resolves the chunked-object limitation; the promoted documented checksum scope uses CRC32C for multiple data requests and MD5 only for one data request. See docs/en/slices/basic-json-contract.md for exact assertion filters and migration destinations.

Obtain authoritative clarification or explicitly authorized service observations of the checked principal, permission recheck timing and condition/permission error ordering before claiming exact provider parity. Do not require a fresh bearer header for possession-authorized session requests or mistake invocation tokens for capability authorization. Keep OPEN and add explicit JSON-OBJECTS-007-PENDING clauses for stored-condition finalization timing and extra-query 400 (wire-tested for PUT ifGenerationMatch) versus ambiguous subsequent-PUT query/header ignoring wording; preserve all existing RSM-FINAL-004/005 local PASS tests, with mutation NotMatch status separately pending under SPEC-008. The SDK POST extension must not be inferred from the PUT wording. BASIC-CONDITION-RESUMABLE is local-only in docs/en/slices/basic-json-contract.md and contributes no new EXACT comparison claim.

gaps.title: Strict authentication error wire details and missing-bucket authorization need real-service evidence

Strict operations recheck the authorized bucket project inside their catalog transaction (a bucket recreated in another project returns 403 without mutation). Bucket IAM now grants permissions through the union of the selected owning project's roles and matching unconditional bucket bindings inside the operation transaction. resolved_research_items.title: Local TLS configuration and Google transport boundary
resolved_research_items.resolution: Checked 2026-10-23: Google request endpoints support HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3; JSON requires HTTPS while XML also supports HTTP. Local TLS settings are emulator configuration, not Discovery/protobuf fields. DESIGN-065 implements HTTPS by default with bundled development certificate/key when both custom paths are absent, optional supplied PEM chain/key, explicit HTTP, TLS 1.2/1.3 and verified client CA/SAN trust for HTTP/1.1. The bundled leaf key is deliberately public local-test material; its public CA is exported by gcs-mimic tls ca and used by HTTPS healthcheck unless --ca-cert selects another root set. The CA private key is not shipped. Unlike the pinned reference's one-sided-path fallback, specifying only one custom path fails startup; invalid supplied pairs never fall back. No open provider TLS contradiction affects this scope; HTTP/2/3, gRPC, public issuance, system trust-store changes, mTLS, reload, proxy origin, signing and dual-listener migration remain separate work. See docs/en/slices/local-tls.md and docs/en/evidence/local-tls.md.
